summary: Madhusudan Kaul Shastri was an Indologist. He served as Superintendent at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, with his tenure attested between 1918 and 1934 and again from 1943 to 1945.
Madhusudan Singh Vats (1896–1972) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji (Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay).

Maggie Bickford is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Bennington College, Yale University, and Princeton University (~1977–1987). She was a Member at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1990–1991) and Professor at Brown University (1993).

Mahadev Govind Ranade (1842–1901) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indologist. He earned his PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University by 2015 and later held a post at the same institution.

Mahasi Sayadaw (1904–1982) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied under U Nārada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw, served as abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung, and was resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha.

Mahendranath Gupta (1854–1932) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Hare School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, he served as a professor at Ripon College and held a post at Surendranath College (~1885–1932).

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021) at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and is attested as Pali Text Society Regional Representative in 2026.

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, with his tenure attested in 1882, 1894, and 1914.

Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Ceylon, Harvard, and Chicago under Wendy Doniger, Frank E. Reynolds, and Diana L. Eck. He held posts at McGill, Colgate, and Bath Spa University.
Mahiro Ito (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021. He has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Otani University (~2004–2008) and served as a visiting researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~2009–2011).
Mai Mishiro is an Indology and Buddhist studies researcher who held posts with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and at Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and under Ryōmin Akizuki, he was a professor at Tsukuba University (~1986–2002) and president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Otani University by 2009 and held appointments at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, Otani University, and the Otani Academic Society.

Makoto Funaoka (born 1946) is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who studied at Meiji University. He served as honorary professor at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017) and part-time lecturer at Komazawa University and The Open University of Japan.

Makoto Kitada is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010) and Osaka University (attested 2026).

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942), Nihon, Toyo, and Kamakura Women's universities, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.

Makoto Yoshimura (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1996–2001) and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (~2006).
Malati J. Shendge (born 1934) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, R. D. Vadekar, and Akira Hirakawa.
